Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border payment functionality appears partially available/being integrated rather than fully live: CBL’s IIPS/Mojaloop announcement states the system will enable integration with PAPSS (Pan-African Payment and Settlement System), and CBL Annual Report 2024 states CBL participated in PAPSS to promote cross-border payments. These indicate cross-border linkage capability/participation but not confirmed fully operational cross-border instant payments for end users.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: IIPS is described as supporting Government-to-Person (G2P) transactions including salaries and social benefits (improving transparency and reducing leakages). Mojaloop statement also notes government payments (salaries/social benefits) will process in seconds rather than days.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: CBL has issued consumer protection and market conduct regulations (Regulation No. CBL/RSD/006/2014) covering disclosure, complaints handling, protection of customer information, and guidance on electronic banking services; additionally, the e-payment services regulations require providers to maintain dispute/complaints resolution desk with recourse to CBL Customer Protection Unit.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No mandatory data breach notification regime identified for Liberia; DLA Piper’s country note states “There is generally no breach notification requirement, nor any dedicated agency or entity to which such notification must be made.”

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: No enacted comprehensive personal data protection law found; multiple references note Liberia lacks a dedicated privacy/data protection law (with only sectoral provisions/policies and a draft personal data protection bill being validated in 2024). Therefore, no general data protection legislation coverage could be confirmed as in force.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: CBL has published key regulatory rulebooks for payment providers (e.g., Mobile Money Regulations 2014; Regulations Concerning the Licensing and Operations of Electronic Payment Services 2020), but no public “scheme rulebook” for IIPS/Pay Na-Na (e.g., participation rules, operating rules) was found as a standalone public document beyond summaries in the CBL magazine; therefore rules appear partially available via regulations rather than a full scheme rulebook.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Liberia’s Inclusive Instant Payments System (IIPS), branded “Pay Na-Na”, was launched on 16 Dec 2025 as a national real-time interoperable payments platform enabling instant transfers across mobile money operators and (intended) wider ecosystem; it is described as a “national digital payment platform regulated and supervised by the Central Bank of Liberia (CBL)” enabling interoperability between banks and mobile money operators.
